analysis.detail: Log4Shell. The telemetry ingest filter logs the inbound X-Device-Id header through log4j-core 2.14.1 with message lookups enabled, so attacker-controlled input reaches the JNDI lookup path. Confirmed reachable by code review and a staged ${jndi:ldap://} probe. Remediation: upgrade to 2.17.1 in release 1.1.0, tracked as CR-4821.

Exploitation requires a Thread Context Map lookup in the logging pattern. log4j2.xml uses only %d %p %c{1} %m%n with no ${ctx:} pattern, and the configuration is baked into the signed device image, so the vulnerable lookup is never evaluated. Configuration reviewed 2026-09-02 by product security.
minimist prototype pollution. The 0.0.8 copy arrived through a transitive build-time dependency that is removed in release 1.1.0; nothing in the shipped runtime imports it.
Prototype pollution in lodash.merge. The device configuration loader merges an operator-supplied JSON profile, so untrusted keys reach merge(). Mitigated by the 4.17.21 upgrade in release 1.1.0.

Command injection via lodash.template. The production bundle is tree-shaken to lodash.get and lodash.merge only; template is absent from the shipped artifact, verified against the 1.0.0 bundle manifest.
ReDoS in the axios trim helper. Assessing whether any attacker-controlled string reaches header parsing on the telemetry upload path. Owner: platform-security. Target date: 2026-09-19.
